0.0.n: A personal pronoun commonly used by boys and men, with a softer feel than 俺.

0.1.n: Marks 僕 as the topic: the sentence tells us about the speaker.

0.2.n: Points to a particular year remembered by the speaker.

0.3.n: Combines with あの to refer to a specific past year.

0.4.n: Links 年 to 夏, specifying which year's summer.

0.5.n: This time expression needs no particle here to tell us when the stay happened.

0.7.n: Used for one's own mother when speaking to others; Japanese leaves out my here.

0.8.n: Here の replaces が to mark 母 as the person who grew up, within a phrase describing 屋敷.

0.9.n: Plain past form of 育つ; 母の育った describes the estate where the mother grew up.

0.10.n: An adjective placed directly before 屋敷 to describe its age.

0.11.n: Refers to a large residence, often including its grounds, rather than just an ordinary house.

0.12.n: Marks the estate as the place where the speaker spent time.

0.14.n: Expresses a duration; 間 indicates a span of time.

0.15.n: Limits the stay to 一週間, emphasizing its short duration.

0.16.n: Plain past form of 過ごす, used here for spending a period of time somewhere.

1.0.n: Refers to the speaker's own mother without explicitly saying my.

1.1.n: Identifies 母 as the person who was speaking.

1.2.n: 言う becomes 言って + いた, presenting the mother's words as something she said in the past.

1.3.n: Short for の; adds a sense of explaining or providing background.

1.4.n: Completes んだ, giving the explanation a casual, matter-of-fact tone.

1.6.n: Modifies 家 and points to the house currently being discussed or indicated.

1.7.n: Combines with この to identify the particular home.

1.8.n: Links 家 to 庭, showing that the garden belongs to the house.

1.9.n: Refers to the outdoor grounds of the house.

1.10.n: Marks the garden as the location where the sighting happened.

1.12.n: Refers to a miniature humanlike being, called a borrower in this story, not specifically a child.

1.13.n: Marks 小人 as what the mother saw.

1.14.n: Plain past form of 見る; the unstated person doing the seeing is the mother.

1.15.n: Casual quotation marker, linking the sighting back to what the mother said.

0.lit: I, that year's summer, at the old estate where my mother grew up, spent only one week.
0.tip: 母の育った comes before 屋敷 to describe it; Japanese puts where someone grew up before the place.

1.lit: My mother used to say, you see: in this house's garden, she saw a tiny person, she said.
1.tip: The final って marks the preceding sighting as the content of the mother's words, even after a sentence break.
